title: malus domestica subsp. pumila
intro: Malus domestica subsp. pumila, commonly known as the dwarf or dessert apple, is a subspecies of apple tree that is naturally smaller in size and compact in growth. This plant has been used for its various health benefits, including its ability to aid in digestion, reduce inflammation, and support immune function. The therapeutic actions of Malus domestica subsp. pumila include its antimicrobial, antidiabetic, and antioxidant properties, which help to protect against oxidative stress and promote overall well-being. The bioactive constituents of this plant include quercetin, catechins, and chlorogenic acid, which are responsible for its therapeutic effects and contribute to its use in traditional medicine.
